comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
As noted by Curious, if a discovery is not listed under these assorted tables, it very likely cannot have an ornament made out of its discovery card (except for a very small number of discoveries not fully updated on the DB, such as Mt. Fuji's ornament coming from Massawa, and King Protea's ornament being produced at Luanda).

I have heard the Chichen Itza quest can be pulled again even if you haven't lost the discovery card, but haven't tried confirming this for myself as of yet. The only way to lose discovery cards like Chichen Itza is to:

- Turn it in at your nation's Caribbean Colony/Lima city official (assuming it's listed; selections change at set intervals)
- Sacrifice it during Treasure Hunt clue synthesis (useable discovery cards change hourly, and every hunt displays a different set of cards)
- Have the card equipped to a Debate card deck and lose during an official tournament (usually held once a month)

Hope that helps. Cheers, and favorable mediator quest generations to you.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
Although most players probably know this, a tip for those that don't who may come by this section... equipment rewards from quests can be displayed at Paris museum, as long as they meet the following criteria:

1. The discovery must come from outside of 'normal and boring' Europe culture zones, the same as any normal ornament.
2. If the equipment reward can be color-customized, it must be left (or changed back) to its default color appearance before you can display it as an ornament in Paris.

Otherwise, anything from Green Dragon Crescent Blade to Feather Hair Ornaments can be displayed at Paris. You can even select mannequin gender with some, if you so wish, not that it affects anything.

Like with other ornaments, the cultural contribution points you receive are equivalent to the star rating of the card tied to the equipment, so keep an eye out on player bazaars; maybe you'll see a good 5* discovery equipment ornament for sale at a low price.
